title: 5am Club
logline: A trail runner walks us through the eight quiet steps between his 4:58 alarm and a ridge-top sunrise. Step four, always before the headlamp goes on, is {{product.name}}.

ingested: a pre-run snack or pick-me-up from the fridge is the classic step four
applied: sunscreen, anti-chafe balm or lip balm at the entry mirror is a real pre-run step
worn: socks, base layers, watches, glasses or shoes put on at the entry bench; gear is what a runner's routine is made of
handheld: earbuds, trackers, soft flasks and phone armbands switched on at the counter
carried: a running vest, belt or small pack loaded and zipped before the door
home: the whole first half is his apartment, so a foam roller, coffee maker, sunrise lamp or mat gets its own spot; large furniture only as a place he sits for thirty seconds
consumable: gels, electrolyte tabs and bars from the cupboard, torn open at the counter

avoid: sleep aids or sedatives (the story is getting out the door awake)
anything a runner should not use right before hard exercise

lore: Wes Tanaka works the repair counter at the only bike shop in Pinecrest Valley, which opens at 9. If the ridge is going to happen, it happens before work.

He is in week 12 of a 16-week plan for his first 50k, the Larch Ridge Ultra on the second Saturday of October. The plan is a hand-drawn grid taped to the fridge, eleven rows crossed out in black marker.
He has topped Larch Ridge 147 times and brings one small grey stone down from the summit cairn each time. The jar by the sink is nearly full.
He has rented the one-bedroom above a closed hardware store for six years. The radiator clanks for the first time each autumn, and it started this week.
Miso, a 14-year-old grey tabby, sleeps on the arm of the couch and does not get up for anyone before 7.

beats.summary: In bed at 4:58 with the phone glowing, he whispers to the tripod: five am, come run with me.
Steps one to three at a clip: feet on the cold floor, a big glass of water at the dark window, the double knot.
Step four slows down: the product alone at its spot, then the product moment, with the name and the benefit.
Steps five to seven speed up again: the headlamp clicks on as the benefit lands, the door opens into the blue dark, the climb by headlamp beam.
Step eight: the ridge at sunrise, headlamp off, the valley in cloud below.
Back to step four's spot in morning light: the product waiting for the viewer, with the tagline.
